verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              हते सुदक्षिणे राजन् वीरे चैव श्रुतायुधे।  जवेनाभ्यद्रवन् पार्थं कुपिताः सैनिकास्तव ॥१॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said When king Sudakshina and the heroic Shrutayudha had been slain, your warriors inflamed with wrath, furiously rushed against the son of Pritha.

verses.sanskrit: अभीषाहाः शूरसेनाः शिबयोऽथ वसातयः।  अभ्यवर्षंस्ततो राजन् शरवर्षैर्धनञ्जयम् ॥२॥
तेषां षष्टिशतानन्यान् प्रामथ्नात् पाण्डवः शरैः।  ते स्म भीताः पलायन्ते व्याघ्रात् क्षुद्रमृगा इव ॥३॥
verses.english: The of Pandu consumed sixty thousands of the these and other warriors, with his arrows; and then the rest greatly frightened, began to fly away like smaller animals flying away from the tiger.

verses.sanskrit: ते निवृत्ताः पुनः पार्थं सर्वतः पर्यवारयन्।  रणे सपत्नान्निघ्नन्तं जिगीषन्तं परान् युधि ॥४॥
verses.english: But soon turning back, they surrounded Partha on all sides, who was slaying his foes in battle and trying to obtain victory over them.

verses.sanskrit: तेषामापततां तूर्णं गाण्डीवप्रेषितैः शरैः।  शिरांसि पातयामास बाहूंश्चापि धनञ्जयः ॥५॥
शिरोभिः पातितैस्तत्र भूमिरासीन्निरन्तरा।  अभ्रच्छायेव चैवासीत् ध्वांक्षगृध्रबलैर्युधि ॥६॥
verses.english: The field of battle was thickly strewn over with felled heads; and fights of vultures and crows and ravens formed its cloudy canopy.

verses.sanskrit: तेषु तूत्साद्यमानेषु क्रोधामर्षसमन्वितौ।  श्रुतायुश्चाच्युतायुश्च धनञ्जयमयुध्यताम् ॥७॥
verses.english: Beholding their troops thus extirpated by Arjuna, Shrutayusha and Achyutayush, excited with rage and fury, began to fight vigorously with the former.

verses.sanskrit: बलिनौ स्पर्धिनौ वीरौ कुलजौ बाहुशालिनौ।  तावेनं शरवर्षाणि सव्यदक्षिणमस्यताम् ॥८॥
त्वरायुक्तौ महाराज प्रार्थयानौ महद्यशः। अर्जुनस्य वधप्रेप्सू पुत्रार्थे तव धन्विनौ ॥९॥
तावर्जुनं सहस्रेण पत्रिणां नतपर्वणाम्।  पूरयामासतुः क्रुद्धौ तटागं जलदौ यथा ॥१०॥
verses.english: Inflamed with rage, they covered Arjuna with a thousand winged shafts of depressed knots, like clouds filling a lake with torrents of rain.

verses.sanskrit: श्रुतायुश्च ततः क्रुद्धस्तोमरेण धनञ्जयम्।  आजघान रथश्रेष्ठः पीतेन निशितेन च ॥११॥
सोऽतिविद्धो बलवता शत्रुणा शत्रुकर्शनः।  जगाम परमं मोहं मोहयन् केशवं रणे ॥१२॥
verses.english: Thus sorely wounded by his powerful adversary, that subduer of the foes viz., Arjuna was overwhelmed with a swoon, confounding thereby Keshava himself.

verses.sanskrit: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु सोऽच्युतायुर्महारथः।  शूलेन भृशतीक्ष्णेन ताडयामास पाण्डवम् ॥१३॥
verses.english: At this crisis that mighty car-warrior Achyutayusha struck the son of Pandu with a trident of exceeding sharpness.

verses.sanskrit: क्षते क्षारं स हि ददौ पाण्डवस्य महात्मनः। पार्थोऽपि भृशसंविद्धो ध्वजयष्टिं समाश्रितः ॥१४॥
ततः सर्वस्य सैन्यस्य तावकस्य विशाम्पते।  सिंहनादो महानासीद्धतं मत्वा धनञ्जयम् ॥१५॥
कृष्णश्च भृशसन्तप्तो दृष्टा पार्थं विचेतनम्।  आश्वासयत्सु हृद्याभिर्वाग्भिस्तत्र धनञ्जयम् ॥१६॥
ततस्तौ रथिनां श्रेष्ठौ लब्धलक्षौ धनञ्जयम्।  वासुदेवं च वार्ष्णेयं शरवर्षैः समन्ततः ॥१७॥
स चक्रकूबररथं साश्वध्वजपताकिनम्।  अदृश्यं चक्रतुर्युद्धे तद‌द्भुतमिवाभवत् ॥१८॥
verses.english: Then those foremost of car-warriors, Shrutayusha and Achyutayush of true aim, scattering their showers of arrows on all sides in that battle, made Dhananjaya and the son Vasudeva of the Vrishni race and their car, carwheels, Kuvaras, steeds, flag-staff and banner, disappear from the view. All this indeed seemed wonderful.

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्याश्वस्तस्तु बीभत्सुः शनकैरिव भारत।  प्रेतराजपुरं प्राप्य पुनः प्रत्यागतो यथा ॥१९॥
verses.english: Then, O Bharata, recovering slowly, like one coming back from a visit to the regions of Death, Vibhatsu.

verses.sanskrit: सञ्छन्नं शरजालेन रथं दृष्ट्वा सकेशवम्।  शत्रू चाभिमुखौ दृष्ट्वा दीप्यमानाविवानलौ ॥२०॥
प्रादुश्चक्रे ततः पार्थः शाक्रमस्त्रं महारथः।  तस्मादासन् सहस्राणि शराणां नतपर्वणाम् ॥२१॥
verses.english: The mighty car-warrior Partha invoked into existence the terrible Shakra weapon. From that weapon issued out thousands of arrows.

verses.sanskrit: ते जघ्नुस्तौ महेष्वासौ ताभ्यां मुक्तांश्च सायकान्।  विचेरुराकाशगताः पार्थबाणविदारिताः ॥२२॥
verses.english: Those arrows then struck those two fierce bowmen Shrutayusha and Achyutayush; and the arrows shot by these latter, being cut-off by those of Partha, began to drop down through the sky.

verses.sanskrit: प्रतिहत्य शरांस्तूर्णं शरवेगेन पाण्डवः।  प्रतस्थे तत्र तत्रैव योधयन् वै महारथान् ॥२३॥
verses.english: Then Pandu's son checking the force of all arrows directed towards him with that of his own shafts, began to run hither and thither over the field encountering mighty car-warriors.

verses.sanskrit: तौ च फाल्गुनबाणौघैर्विबाहुशिरसौ कृतौ। वसुधामन्वपद्येतां वातनुन्नाविव द्रुमौ ॥२४॥
verses.english: Then those two heroes deprived of their arms and heads, by the arrows of Arjuna, fell down on the carth like mighty trees broken down by the wind.

verses.sanskrit: श्रुतायुषश्च निधनं वधश्चैवाच्युतायुषः। लोकविस्मापनमभूत्समुद्रस्येव शोषणम् ॥२५॥
verses.english: The slaughter of Shrutayusha and Achyutayush caused a surprise like to what men would fell if the ocean be dried up.

verses.sanskrit: तयोः पदानुगान् हत्वा पुनः पञ्चाशतं रथान्।  प्रत्यगाद्भारतीं सेनां निघ्नन् पार्थो वरान् वरान् ॥२६॥
verses.english: Then, having slain fifty car-warriors, the followers of those two princes, Pritha's son plunged into the army of the Bharatas, crushing down numerous elephants and warriors (at each step).

verses.sanskrit: श्रुतायुषं च निहतं प्रेक्ष्य चैवाच्युतायुषम्। नियतायुश्च सङ्क्रुद्धो दीर्घायुश्चैव भारत ॥२७॥
पुत्रौ तयोर्नरश्रेष्ठौ कौन्तेयं प्रतिजग्मतुः।  किरन्तौ विविधान्बाणान्पितृव्यसनकर्शितौ ॥२८॥
तावर्जुनो मुहूर्तेन शरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः।  प्रैषयत् परमक्रुद्धो यमस्य सदनं प्रति ॥२९॥
लोडयन्तमनीकानि द्विपं पद्मसरो यथा।  नाशक्नुवन्वारयितुं पार्थं क्षत्रियपुङ्गवाः ॥३०॥
verses.english: Then the foremost Kshatriyas of your army were not able to oppose Pritha's son who had been agitating the troops like an elephant agitating a lake over-grown with lotuses.

verses.sanskrit: अङ्गास्तु गजवारेण पाण्डवं पर्यवारयन्।  क्रुद्धाः सहस्रशो राजन् शिक्षिता हस्तिसादिनः ॥३१॥
verses.english: Then thousands of well-trained elephant riders belonging to the divisions of the Angas, excited with rage, O king, surrounded the son of Pandu, with their elephant forces.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्योधनसमादिष्टाः कुञ्जरैः पर्वतोपमैः।  प्राच्याश्च दाक्षिणात्याश्च कलिङ्गप्रमुखा नृपाः ॥३२॥
verses.english: Commanded by Duryodhana, the easterners, the southerners and other kings hearded by the ruler of the Kalingas surrounded Arjuna with their elephants huge as hills.

verses.sanskrit: तेषामापततां शीघ्रं गाण्डीवप्रेषितैः शरैः।  निचकर्त शिरांस्युग्रो बाहूनपि सुभूषणान् ॥३३॥
verses.english: But with the arrows shot from his Gandiva bow, Aruna quickly cut-off their heads and arms decked with ornaments, as they were rushing against him.

verses.sanskrit: तैः शिरोभिर्मही कीर्णां बाहुभिश्च सहाङ्गदैः। बभौ कनकपाषाणा भुजगैरिव संवृता ॥३४॥
verses.english: Strewn over with their heads and arms decked with Angadas, the Earth appeared as if covered with golden stones and numerous snakes.

verses.sanskrit: बाहवो विशिखैश्छिन्नाः शिरांस्युन्मथितानि च। पतमानान्यदृश्यन्त द्रुमेभ्य इव पक्षिणः ॥३५॥
शरैः सहस्रशो विद्धा द्विपाः प्रसृतशोणिताः। अदृश्यन्ताद्रयः काले गैरिकाम्बुस्रवा इव ॥३६॥
निहताः शेरते स्मान्ये बीभत्सोर्निशितैः शरैः। गजपृष्ठगता म्लेच्छा नानाविकृतदर्शनाः ॥३७॥
verses.english: Others slain by the whetted arrows of Vibhatsu, lay prostrate on the field of battle. Numerous Mlechhas, riding on the backs of elephants, of ugly appearances.

verses.sanskrit: नानावेषधरा राजन् नानाशस्त्रौघसंवृताः। रुधिरेणानुलिप्ताङ्गा भान्ति चित्रैः शरैर्हताः ॥३८॥
verses.english: Attired in various kinds of garments and, O king, armed with numerous weapons and weltering in blood, appeared beautiful, as they lay on the ground deprived of life by means of various kinds of shafts.

verses.sanskrit: शोणितं निर्वमन्ति स्म द्विपाः पार्थशराहताः।  सहस्रशश्छिन्नगात्राः सारोहाः सपदानुगाः ॥३९॥
verses.english: Thousands of elephants with their bodies mangled and their riders and those who followed them, having been struck with the arrows of Pritha's son, vomitted blood.

verses.sanskrit: चिच्छेदेन्द्रध्वजाकारौ शिरश्चान्येन पत्रिणा। स पपात हतो राजन् वसुधामनुनादयन् ॥३९॥
verses.english: Thousands of elephants with their bodies mangled and their riders and those who followed them, having been struck with the arrows of Pritha's son, vomitted blood.

verses.sanskrit: चुक्रुशुश्च निपेतुश्च बभ्रमुश्चापरे दिशः।  भृशं त्रस्ताश्च बहवः स्वानेव ममृदुर्गजाः ॥४०॥
सान्तरायुधिनश्चैव द्विपांस्तीक्ष्णविषोपमाः। विदन्त्यसुरमायां ये सुघोरा घोरचक्षुषः ॥४१॥
verses.english: Many other elephants armed with weapons and fierce like snakes of virulent poison, also did the same. Numerous furious Yavanas, Paradas, Shakas, Balhikas and Mlechhas born of the cow (of Vasishtha) possessed of fearful eyes, accomplished in smitting, looking like emissaries of Death, all versed in the use of illusive powers of the Asuras.

verses.sanskrit: यवनाः पारदाश्चैव शकाश्च सह बाह्लिकैः।  काकवर्णा दुराचाराः स्त्रीलोलाः कलहप्रियाः ॥४२॥
द्राविडास्तत्र युध्यन्ते मत्तमातङ्गविक्रमाः।  गोयोनिप्रभवा म्लेच्छाः कालकल्पाः प्रहारिणः ॥४३॥
दार्वातिसारा दरदाः पुण्ड्राश्चैव सहस्रशः।  ते न शक्याः स्म सङ्ख्यातुं व्राताः शतसहस्रशः ॥४४॥
अभ्यवर्षन्त ते सर्वे पाण्डवं निशितैः शरैः। अवाकिरंश्च ते म्लेच्छा नानायुद्धविशारदाः ॥४५॥
तेषामपि ससर्जाशु शरवृष्टिं धनञ्जयः। सृष्टिस्तथाविधाह्यासीच्छलभानामिवायतिः ॥४६॥
verses.english: Dhananjaya also poured his arrows or them in quick succession, and the arrows discharged from the Gandiva bow appeared like fights of locusts, as they flew through the air.

verses.sanskrit: अभ्रच्छायामिव शरैः सैन्ये कृत्वा धनञ्जयः। मुण्डार्धमुण्डाञ्जटिलानशुचीञ्जटिलाननान् ॥४७॥
म्लेच्छानशातयत्सर्वान् समेतानस्त्रतेजसा। शरैश्च शतशो विद्धास्ते सङ्घा गिरिचारिणः। प्राद्रवन्त रणे भीता गिरिगह्वरवासिनः ॥४८॥
गजाश्वसादिम्लेच्छानां पतितानां शितै शरैः। बकाः कङ्का वृका भूमावपिबन् रुधिरं मुदा। पत्त्यश्वरथनागैश्च प्रच्छन्नकृतसङ्क्रमाम् ॥४९॥
शरवर्षप्लवां घोरां केशशैवलशाद्वलाम्। प्रावर्तयन्नदीमुग्रां शोणितौघतरङ्गिणीम् ॥५०॥
verses.bhavadeepa: प्रच्छन्नेन प्रच्छादनेन कृतो रचितः संक्रमो यस्याम् ॥४९॥

verses.sanskrit: छिन्नाङ्गुलीक्षुद्रमत्स्यां युगान्ते कालसन्निभाम्। प्राकरोद्गजसम्बाधां नदीमुत्तरशोणिताम् ॥५१॥
देहेभ्यो राजपुत्राणां नागाश्वरथसादिनाम्।  यथास्थलं च निम्नं च न स्याद्वर्षति वासवे ॥५२॥
तथासीत् पृथिवी सर्वां शोणितेन परिप्लुता।  षट्सहस्त्राह्नयान्वीरान् पुनर्दशशतान् वरान् ॥५३॥
verses.english: Its uplands and low-lands could not be distinguished, as if Vasava had poured a torrent of rain over it.

verses.sanskrit: प्राहिणोन्मृत्युलोकाय क्षत्रियान् क्षत्रियर्षभः।  शरैः सहस्रशो विद्धा विधिवत्कल्पिता द्विपाः ॥५४॥
verses.english: Six thousand brave warriors and many other Kshatriyas were dispatched by that foremost of Kshatriya Arjuna as to the abode of Death.

verses.sanskrit: शेरते भूमिमासाद्य शैला वज्रहता इव।  सवाजिरथमातङ्गान्निघ्नन् व्यचरदर्जुनः ॥५५॥
verses.english: Thousands of elephants equipped according to rule, being pierced with numerous arrows. Lay prostrate on the field like so many mountains struck down by the thunder bolt. Then Arjuna careered over the field slaying horses, car-warriors and elephants. Like an elephant in rut crushing a forest of reeds.

verses.sanskrit: प्रभिन्न इव मातङ्गो मृद्नन्नलवनं यथा।  भूरिद्रुमलतागुल्मं शुष्केन्धनतृणोलपम् ॥५६॥
निर्दहेदनलोऽरण्यं यथा वायुसमीरितः।  सेनारण्यं तव तथा कृष्णानिलसमीरितः ॥५७॥
verses.english: Just as fire helped forwarded by the wind, burns down a forest abounding in trees, creepers, brush-woods, dry fuels and grass, so, that fire viz., the enraged Dhananjaya, the son of Pandu, having arrows for his flames and helped forward by the Krishna-wind, consumed the forest constituted by your troops.

verses.sanskrit: इन्द्रध्वज इवोत्सृष्टो यन्त्रनिर्मुक्तबन्धनः।  रथानीकावगाढश्च वारणाश्वशतैर्वृतः।  अदृश्यत तदा पार्थो घनैः सूर्य इवावृतः ॥५७॥
verses.english: Just as fire helped forwarded by the wind, burns down a forest abounding in trees, creepers, brush-woods, dry fuels and grass, so, that fire viz., the enraged Dhananjaya, the son of Pandu, having arrows for his flames and helped forward by the Krishna-wind, consumed the forest constituted by your troops.

verses.sanskrit: शरार्चिरदहत् क्रुद्धः पाण्डवाग्निर्धनञ्जयः।  शून्यान् कुर्वन् रथोपस्थान् मानवैः संस्तरन् महीम् ॥५८॥
प्रानृत्यदिव सम्बाधे चापहस्तो धनञ्जयः।  वज्रकल्पैः शरैर्भूमिं कुर्वन्नुत्तरशोणिताम् ॥५९॥
प्राविशद्भारतीं सेनां सङ्क्रुद्धो वै धनञ्जयः।  तं श्रुतायुस्तथाम्बष्ठो व्रजमानं न्यवारयत् ॥६०॥
verses.english: Deluging the ground with blood drawn by means of shafts resembling the thunderbolt itself. Dhananjaya, inflamed with wrath, plunged deep into the ranks of the Bharata troops. When he thus advancing, Shrutayudha the ruler of the Ambashtha's then opposed him.

verses.sanskrit: तस्यार्जुनः शरैस्तीक्ष्णैः कङ्कपत्रपरिच्छदैः।  न्यपातयद्धयान् शीघ्रं यतमानस्य मारिष ॥६१॥
verses.english: Thereupon, O sire, when he was thus exerting himself against Arjuna, the latter with sharp arrows furnished with wings made of Kanka feathers, speedily cut down his horses.

verses.sanskrit: धनुश्चास्यापरैश्छित्त्वा शरैः पार्थो विचक्रमे।  अम्बष्ठस्तु गदां गृह्य कोपपर्याकुलेक्षणः ॥६२॥
verses.english: was Then with other arrows cutting off his bow, Arjuna began to career over the field. Thereat the ruler of the Ambashthas, with eyes rolling in rage, took up his mace.

verses.sanskrit: आससाद रणे पार्थं केशवं च महारथम्।  ततः सम्प्रहरन् वीरो गदामुद्यम्य भारत॥६३॥
verses.english: And assaulted in that battle Pritha's son and also the mighty car-warrior Keshava. Then O Bharata that hero, up-lifting and striking with his mace.

verses.sanskrit: रथमावार्य गदया केशवं समताडयत्।  गदया ताडितं दृष्ट्वा केशवं परवीरहा ॥६४॥
verses.english: Checked the progress of Arjuna's car and with it began to strike Keshava; beholding Keshava struck with the mace, that slayer of hostile heroes.

verses.sanskrit: अर्जुनोऽथ भृशं क्रुद्धः सोम्बष्ठं प्रति भारत। ततः शरैर्हेमपुङ्खैः सगदं रथिनां वरम् ॥६५॥
verses.english: Arjuna, O Bharata, excited to the highest pitch of anger, showered over that foremost of car-warriors viz., the ruler of the Ambasthas wielding the mace, numerous shafts furnished with golden wings, like the mass of clouds enshrouding the risen sin. Thereafter with other arrows, Pritha's son splintered into pieces the mace of that illustrious warrior; indeed this feat appeared to be marvellous. Then beholding that mace of his cut down and taking up another heavy one.

verses.sanskrit: छा‌दयामास समरे मेघः सूर्यमिवोदितम्।  अथापरैः शरैश्चापि गदां तस्य महात्मनः ॥६६॥
अचूर्णयत् तदा पार्थस्तद‌द्भुतमिवाभवत्।  अथ तां पतितां दृष्ट्वा गृह्यान्यां च महागदाम् ॥६७॥
अर्जुनं वासुदेवं च पुनः पुनरताडयत्। तस्यार्जुनः क्षुरप्राभ्यां सगदावुद्यतौ भुजौ ॥६८॥
verses.english: The ruler of the Ambashthas began to strike Vasudeva's son and Arjuna, incessantly. Thereat Arjuna with a couple of razor-headed arrows cut-off his upraised arms weilding the pole of Indra; and then with another winged shaft be cut off his head. Then that king, O monarch, fell down on the earth creating a loud noise.
